member_of.name: The Flamingos (original group that became The Platters)
Herb Reed's Platters (formed his own group)

podcast.title: Recipient of Name Rights (2011)
podcast.body: In 2011, after decades of legal battles, a judge finally ruled that Herb Reed held the legitimate rights to The Platters' name, and that "Five Platters Inc." had never legally owned it. "A judge finally ruled that Herb Read had the rights to the name, and that five platters ink had never owned the name."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Death in 2012
podcast.body: Herb Reed passed away in 2012, shortly after the court ruling that granted him the rights to The Platters' name. However, the company he licensed the name to continues to license a band to tour as The Platters. "Herb Read died in 2012, shortly afterwards, though the company he licensed the name to, still licenses a band to tour as the platters."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Conspiracy Allegation in Alex Hodge's Departure
podcast.body: Gaynell Hodge claimed that Herb Reed conspired with Book Ram to orchestrate Alex Hodge's departure from The Platters, citing Alex's suspicion of Ram's business practices as the true motive, rather than the official reason of marijuana possession. "Ram and Herb Reed conspired to get rid of Alex."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Last Classic Member to Leave
podcast.body: Herb Reed was the final member of The Platters' classic lineup to remain with the group, eventually leaving by 1969, after which Book Ram's companies continued with groups having no original members. "By 1969, Herb Reed was the only member of the classic lineup still in the group, and then he left the group too."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Lead Vocals on First Ram Single
podcast.body: Unusually, Herb Reed, rather than the regular lead singer Tony Williams, was featured on lead vocals for both sides of The Platters' first single released after signing with Book Ram. This experiment did not prove successful. "The first single they released after signing with Ram was one which, rather oddly, featured Herb Reed on lead vocals on both sides, rather than their normal lead Sony Williams."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
